# A lower bound of a ball as a limb, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_lower_as_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A lower bound of the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$, as a number of `T`:

$$l \le x \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.lower_as<T>()` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `T` | `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- When every operand and $l$ are finite, the statement on finite operands holds:
    - $\lvert l - (c - r)\rvert \le 5\,u\,(\lvert c\rvert + \lvert r\rvert) + 3\,\eta$.
- If the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is empty: $l = +\infty$.
- Otherwise $l \le x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line gives $l = -\infty$.
- No number of steps of `T` from $\mathrm{RD}(c - r)$ is claimed: the center, of two limbs, is rounded to `T` before the radius is subtracted, which moves the bound by up to one gap of `T` at $c$, and when $c - r$ is much smaller than $c$ in magnitude (a radius close to $\lvert c\rvert$) that is many gaps of `T` at the result. What is claimed of the distance is that $l$ is on its side of every member and within the bound above: $\lvert l - (c - r)\rvert \le 5\,u\,(\lvert c\rvert + \lvert r\rvert) + 3\,\eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u$ | $5 \cdot 2^{-53} \approx 5.5511 \times 10^{-16}$ | $5 \cdot 2^{-24} \approx 2.9802 \times 10^{-7}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-1074} \approx 1.4822 \times 10^{-323}$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-149} \approx 4.2039 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.4p-51`, `0x1.8p-1073` | `0x1.4p-22f`, `0x1.8p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_lower_as_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_lower_as_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_lower_as_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the center rounded down, minus the radius, rounded down (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_lower_as_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_lower_as_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`to_down_2`](to_down_2.md), [`sub_down_1`](sub_down_1.md).

```
# The lower bound of a ball with a 2-limb center, as a number of T (milestone2.md, "One
# enclosure interface", the row of lower_as and upper_as, and "The empty set and the whole line"):
# the center rounded down to T by to_down_2, then the radius subtracted, rounded down. A bound on
# its side of every member: the whole line gives -inf, the empty ball +inf. For a finite ball
# it is less than one gap of T at c plus one gap at the result away from c - r; no number of
# steps from the directed rounding of c - r bounds it, since c - r can be far smaller than c in
# magnitude. What is claimed of the distance is the error entry: at most 5 u (|c| + r) + 3 eta,
# from the two gaps, each at most max(2 u |t|, eta), and |t| <= |c| + r + 2 u |c| + eta for the
# number t that the second rounding rounds.

a  = to_down_2(c0, c1)
t  = sub_down_1(a, r)
ne = eq(r, r)
l  = select(ne, t, const inf)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_lower_as_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | 0.800000 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | 0.800000 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 712 620 | 0 | 0.799044 (`fp:4:-8:3`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- Which canonical value comes out when an operand is not finite: the claims say only that it is canonical.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
